paper.paper_scope: Overview of high-aluminum low-density steels for automotive lightweighting, covering the effect of Al on density, CALPHAD thermodynamic modeling of Fe-Al-C/Fe-Mn-Al-C systems, microstructural evolution in ferritic, two-phase austenite-ferrite and austenitic TRIPLEX grades, microstructure-property relations, and weight-saving potential versus DP600.
paper.title: Low-Density Steels: Complex Metallurgy for Automotive Applications

unmapped_findings: High-aluminum additions give density reductions of 8-10% or higher compared with low-carbon steels (b0004).
The paper classifies high-Al automotive steels into three families: ferritic Fe-Al alloys, two-phase austenite-ferrite alloys, and austenitic TRIPLEX alloys (b0032).
The kappa-phase (j-phase) is an ordered perovskite-type carbide with formula (Fe,Mn)3AlCx and E21 Strukturbericht designation (b0021).
